picks.title: This New AI Music Model Is Already Better Than Suno—We Put ACE to the Test
picks.rationale: New model release: ACE Studio's ACE Music v1 tops the Artificial Analysis blind vocal-music leaderboard over Suno v6, with hands-on test results creators can act on.
picks.excerpt: ACE Studio's ACE Music v1 took first place on Artificial Analysis' blind vocal-music leaderboard (1,160 Elo vs Suno v6's 1,144); Decrypt's tests found stronger melodies, more natural vocals and cleaner endings, though Suno handled niche genres better.

picks.title: MusicFlux: Flexible Conditioning for Text-Guided Music Generation and Editing
picks.rationale: New research release: MusicFlux turns a pretrained flow-matching text-to-audio model into a text-guided music editor (inpainting, event insertion, restoration), with two conditioning modes that trade edit quality against compute.
picks.excerpt: MusicFlux is a text-guided music editor built on a pretrained flow-matching text-to-audio model, with two conditioning approaches that trade editing quality against compute for inpainting, event insertion and restoration.

picks.title: Idol’s Labelcamp and startup MyPart explore AI connections
picks.rationale: New product: Labelcamp's AI Connector lets labels and distributors run supply-chain ops and catalogue analytics from Claude or ChatGPT, agentic AI reaching music distribution back-office.
picks.excerpt: Idol's distribution-management platform Labelcamp launched an AI Connector letting labels and distributors run supply-chain operations and catalogue analytics from Claude or ChatGPT; startup MyPart also added agentic AI connections.

picks.title: We Distributed Cloned AI Music From a Fake Nigerian Artist
picks.rationale: Original investigation: an outlet openly submitted a voice-cloned AI track from a fake artist and documented which distributors let it through, new evidence on distribution safeguards.
picks.excerpt: Investigation: the outlet built a fake Nigerian artist with a cloned voice and an AI-generated song, told distribution platforms exactly what it had done, and tracked which ones still distributed it.

picks.title: Nvidia Moves to Quash Burdensome UMG v. Suno Subpoena
picks.rationale: New court filing in the UMG v. Suno training-data case: Nvidia's motion to quash a deposition subpoena after producing 6,300+ documents pulls the chipmaker into the discovery fight.
picks.excerpt: Nvidia moved to quash a 'burdensome' deposition subpoena in UMG v. Suno, saying it has already produced more than 6,300 documents.

https://www.digitalmusicnews.com/2026/11.new_action: Nvidia filed a motion to quash a deposition subpoena in UMG v. Suno (new third-party filing, 2026-11-11).
